references.text: God is called as a witness between two parties entering an agreement, just as the elders of Gilead invoke the Lord as a witness between them and Jephthah.
The Lord is invoked as a witness between Abraham and Abimelech in their covenant, just as the Lord here is a witness between the elders of Gilead and Jephthah.
Samuel invokes the Lord as a witness when he confirms an agreement with the people, similar to how the elders of Gilead invoke the Lord as a witness.
The Lord is described as the one who hears and knows, just as the elders of Gilead confess that the Lord will hear and be a witness to their vow.
The continuation of the story where Jephthah goes with the elders and the people make him leader and commander in Mizpah before the Lord.
The sons of Gad and Reuben promise to do as the Lord has said, corresponding to the elders of Gilead's pledge to act according to Jephthah's words.
